text:
Raj Patel: Heads up — saw a regression in A100 batch perf after the kernel-selector tweak. p99 latency for long-seq routes is ~+15%, and KV cache hit rate dipped ~8%. Planted a profiler but wanted to flag here before digging deeper.
infra-bot: ALERT: perf_regression_detected /runtime/batch_latency p99 +15% (alert_id=a100-regress-3887654321)
Alisa Chen: Seen the traces — kernel_selector flipped to kernel_v2 for sequences >1024. v2 uses the large-GEMM path, packing looks different. Sharing flame graphs in a sec.
Matt Green: Can you paste the profiler commands / config used? curious if this is workspace / scratch limit related or a pure kernel perf change. Also what's max_tokens_per_batch on the affected pools?
Raj Patel: Profiler snippet and the pool config we observed: ```
profiler: nvprof --sample=sm_action --trace-mem
device_profile: a100-80gb
max_tokens_per_batch: 131072
kernel_selector: auto-v2
kv_cache_mode: dynamic_prefix
batch_formation: continuous
queue_policy: balanced
```
Sana Iqbal: I ran a short microbench swapping max_tokens_per_batch to 65536 vs 131072. With 65k we get the old baseline numbers. With 131k we hit kernel_v2 and p99 jumps. Hypothesis: larger token budgets encourage bigger slices which trigger v2 that has worse occupancy for typical batch shapes we get on production.
Alisa Chen: FWIW we also see KV fragmentation: when slices grow, KV entries scatter across more slots causing more cache misses. That 8% drop in kv_hit matches the latency bump. We should check cache partitioning per slot and whether cross-request invalidation is happening.
Matt Green: Two quick experiments to run: (1) force kernel_selector=auto-v1 on canary A100 nodes, (2) limit max_tokens_per_batch=80k to see tradeoff. Can infra spin up a canary patch?
infra-bot: Canary job created: canary/a100-kernel-affinity-3887654321 by Matt Green. job_id=job-20260318-77. Nodes: a100-pool-canary-03.
Sana Iqbal: I'll run the kernel_override env and push a 2-hour microbench. Will collect p50/p95/p99, kv_hit, and packing distribution.
benchie-bot: Perf-run summary (quick): 
- baseline (v1, 65k): p99=210ms, kv_hit=90%, avg_pack=12 tokens/request
- v2 + 131k: p99=242ms (+15%), kv_hit=82%, avg_pack=18 tokens/request
- v1 + 131k: p99=215ms, kv_hit=89%
=> quick takeaway: v2 with large max_tokens increases packing but reduces KV locality and hurts p99.
Alisa Chen: Proposed mitigation: for A100 default max_tokens_per_batch -> 80k (down from 131k) and adjust kernel_selector seq_len cutoff: kernel_v2 only for seq_len > 1536 (was 2048/1024 boundary that changed). Also add a KV-aware feature flag to the selector so we prefer kernels that preserve KV locality for continuous batching.
Raj Patel: Sounds reasonable. Also let's consider queue_policy: continuous merging of long requests leads to tail amplification. Try queue_policy=strict_slots on the canary to prevent long+short mixing.
Matt Green: I'll open a PR with two changes: (1) default a100 max_tokens_per_batch=80000, (2) kernel_selector threshold tweak + unit tests + canary rollout plan. Draft PR: https://git.internal/repo/pulls/1234 (WIP). Will include a canary rollout doc and rollback steps.
Sana Iqbal: After canary finishes, I'll validate small-seq workloads (chat, short completions) and embedding routes — want to ensure we didn't regress other card classes.
Alisa Chen: Also adding a lightweight regression test: synthetic packing sim that models continuous batching + kv cache behavior. If PR passes canary we flip feature flag gradually.
Raj Patel: Great. Assigning owners: Matt -> PR and rollout, Sana -> canary bench & metrics, Alisa -> selector change + tests. I'll own post-mortem notes and perf dashboard updates. :thumbsup:
Matt Green: ack, i'll tag infra and eng-sre on the rollout doc.
infra-bot: Canary completed: job-20260318-77 finished. Results uploaded to /perf/canaries/a100-kernel-affinity/3887654321.
benchie-bot: Final canary numbers: recommended config (v1 + 80k cap) restores baseline p99 within +/-2% and kv_hit=~89%.
Alisa Chen: I'll follow up with a tiny follow-up PR to add KV-awareness to the selector heuristics (heuristic param: prefer_kernel_locality=true).
Raj Patel: Thanks all — seems like kernel affinity + token budget was the root cause. We'll monitor dashboards for 48h after rollout.
Matt Green: filing the rollout ticket now, linking PR and canary artifacts. https://tickets.internal/INF-867
Sana Iqbal: leaving a note: keep an eye on mixed packing on L4/T4 pools too — different kernels might behave differently there.
Raj Patel: Good call. We'll run similar guarded experiments on L4/T4 next week.
